frequency_question: How often do central bank boards with active CCyB frameworks choose to lift the buffer above zero when economic conditions permit?
membership_rule: Includes developed market central banks with operational CCyB frameworks (e.g., Fed, BoE, ECB/Eurosystem national authorities, RBA, RBNZ) evaluated across economic cycles; excludes jurisdictions without an active framework.

cases.name: Bank of England FPC CCyB hikes (2016-2018)
Reserve Bank of New Zealand CCyB increases
US Federal Reserve Board CCyB decisions

coverage_note: International peers show frequent activation, but US Federal Reserve leadership has historically shown zero institutional will to deploy this specific tool.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller emerging markets with nascent macroprudential frameworks.
skeleton: Active CCyB jurisdictions evaluated across post-Basel III implementation cycles
multiplier: Multiple major jurisdictions have utilized non-zero CCyBs, but the US Federal Reserve specifically has maintained its CCyB at 0.0% since the framework's inception, reflecting a distinct institutional preference for relying on stress testing over the active deployment of the CCyB.
validity_reason: Macroprudential governance frameworks and institutional preferences of central bank boards change slowly over multi-year horizons.
